title: Voltplay to Present Its New UFO-Themed Crash Game at SBC Summit 2026
excerpt: Voltplay today announced that it will present its new crash game, WTF: What’s That Flying?, at SBC Summit 2026 in Lisbon.
content:
Voltplay today announced that it will present its new crash game, WTF: What’s That Flying?, at SBC Summit 2026 in Lisbon. The new game combines fast-paced crash mechanics with a humorous UFO theme, placing players behind the controls of a flying saucer navigating the streets of New York during Independence Day celebrations. As the multiplier and tension rise with every passing second, players must decide when to cash out before a random firework, street hazard, or unexpected obstacle turns the alien heist into a smoking disaster.

A decision must be made every second: cash out and leave the round in time, or keep risking it for a bigger reward. Four difficulty levels let players choose the right pace, from more cautious gameplay to complete chaos. Clear rules, simple controls, dynamic gameplay, and a humorous sci-fi presentation make WTF: What’s That Flying? easy to learn but difficult to master.

The vibrant arcade style transports players to a festive New York, where the hustle and bustle of the city collides with an absurd alien mission. Fireworks, sudden hazards, and a visually striking UFO create a sense of movement and unpredictability. The game is built around the contrast between a colorful festive atmosphere and an increasingly dangerous flight. This turns every round into a short comedic chase for a higher multiplier.

Key Features

  • Crash mechanics with a constant choice: The player can lock in their winnings at any time or continue the round to increase the potential reward.
  • Four difficulty levels: Different modes allow players to adjust the intensity of the game to match their personal appetite for risk.
  • Escalating danger: The longer the UFO remains in flight, the higher the tension and the likelihood that the round will end prematurely.
  • Unpredictable events: Random fireworks, road hazards, and sudden obstacles can change the outcome of the flight.
  • A humorous alien theme: The classic logic of crash games gets an unusual twist. Instead of sending a spaceship into action, the player sends a UFO on a heist.
  • Fast-paced format: Dynamic rounds are well suited to short gaming sessions and the “just one more round” experience.

RTP: 95.5%

Volatility: Depends on the selected difficulty level.

Maximum Win: Up to x72,432.

Status: Live / Crash.

Availability: A demo version is available on the official game page: https://games.voltplay.dev/wtf/

The parameters listed above apply to the published version of the game and should be considered together with the rules of the relevant operator, its terms of use, and any applicable jurisdictional restrictions.

Format: Browser-based game with Desktop and Mobile versions.

Languages: English, Spanish, Ukrainian, Portuguese, and Russian.

Demo Mode: Available via the Play Demo button.

WTF: What’s That Flying? stands out thanks to its distinctive character and instantly recognizable premise: a UFO is attempting to carry out an alien heist over festive New York while the player decides when it is time to disappear with the loot. Four difficulty levels expand the product’s potential use cases, while the combination of clear crash mechanics, escalating risk, and random obstacles creates a compelling reason to keep coming back to the game.

Three elements are particularly important for promotional communications: the comedic UFO theme, the festive Fourth of July visual context, and the high maximum win potential of up to x72,432. As a result, the game may appeal to operators looking for a fast-paced, visually distinctive, and easy-to-explain crash product with a strong identity and memorable atmosphere.

About VoltPlay

VoltPlay is a casino game studio creating bright, dynamic products for the international iGaming industry. The company develops games for players, streamers, and operators, combining clear mechanics, distinctive visual identities, and memorable on-screen moments. Its portfolio spans slots, crash, wheel, and arcade experiences, built around the principles of Provably Fair, Mobile-First, Streamer-Friendly, and Fast Iterations.
